raw.cause: With COCKPIT_FAULT=deadlock, gps_handle() sends MSG_HINT to nav (event 63971) while it is still holding nav's unreplied MSG_POSITION request (63860/63870). nav's only thread is REPLY-blocked in MsgSend on gps, so it can never MsgReceive the hint. gps stays SEND-blocked on nav (-63972) and nav stays REPLY-blocked on gps (-63861): a send cycle the contract forbids (gps may send to no one), and it ends in deadlock.
raw.qnx_call: MsgSend in gps (gps_handle -> ask(gps_nav, MSG_HINT)) to nav while nav is blocked in MsgSend to gps
raw.fix_summary: Remove the gps -> nav call. gps must reply to MSG_POSITION from its own state and never send to nav. Messages must flow only down the allowed graph (nav -> gps). If gps really needs nav's route data, nav should push it in its own request, for example as a field of MSG_POSITION. Do not change the contract: allowing gps -> nav would reintroduce the cycle.

finding: gps talks to nav, which the contract does not allow
